text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
VJESNIK
- President Franjo Tudjman opened a desulphurisation at national oil firm INA's Rijeka refinery aimed to reduce sulphur in diesel fuel by 20 percent. The investment totalled 500 million kuna.
- Building of a motorway to link Zagreb and Adriatic port of Split is to start this year with the help of foreign investors, says Reconstruction Minister Jure Radic.
- German industrial gaint Daimler-Benz is considering taking part in the construction of road infrastructure in Croatia and is particularly interested in building an airport on the island of Hvar.
- Experts have completed exhumation of a mass grave in a central Croatian village of Bacin. The grave contained bodies of 56 villagers killed by Serb rebel forces in 1991.

- Independent democratic Serb party (SDSS) has nominated 610 candidates to run in the local elections in the Osijek and Vukovar counties on April 13. Vojislav Stanimirovic, SDSS president, is to head all slates.
- According to U.N. figures, there are 126,876 registered voters in Eastern Slavonia of which 53 percent are Croats, 30 percent Serbs, seven percent Hungarians and 10 percent others.

- The World Bank is expected to approve a $100 million loan to help Croatia overhaul its banks and is also preparing a $80 million loan to back reform of the country's pension system, says Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa, who is on a U.S. tour.
- U.S. corporation Bechtel Group is planning to invest some $600 million in road construction in Croatia, says Bechtel's head Adrian Zaccari after meeting PM Matesa.
- Commercial bank Varazdinska Banka signed an agreement to list its ordinary and preferred shares with a total face value of 175 million kuna on Zagreb's bourse.
- Adriatic tourist town of Dubrovnik expects to record between 800,000 and one million overnights this summer.
VECERNJI LIST

- Selection and appointment of a new Croatian archbishop to succeed Cardinal Franjo Kuharic entered the last phase, but the church authorities are still silent on the issue. The candidate is said already to have been approved by the Pope.
- Japan's Export-Import Bank JEXIM is to visit Croatia in May to decide on a possible investment in Croatia, JEXIM's deputy governor Akiro Nambaro said after meeting a Croatian delegation in Tokyo.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- German car maker Audi plans to manufacture cars in TLM, metal factory in the Dalmatian town of Sibenik, says county prefect Pasko Bubal. Total investment is put at more than 180 million marks.
- Easter holidays have shown the coming tourist season can be much more succesful than in the past years. The island of Hvar is expecting 200,000 overnights this year.
- A six-day Zagreb Auto Show, the biggest car industry exhibition of the kind ever held in Zagreb, will host 586 exhibitors. It opens on April 7.

- "Get ready because I will lead the first train to Vukovar in no more than a few weeks," president Tudjman tells voters during his pre-election campaign in the port of Rijeka. -- Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
